A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study despite the CoScene-to-AIScene renaming. All pages, equations, tables, and figures support comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original SemanticKITTI and nuScenes segmentation results, component ablations, and augmentation and sensitivity experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds backbone evaluation, qualitative segmentation comparisons, and point-erasure diagnostics.

M1.justification: The teacher-student pipeline, point erasure, patch pools, MixPatch, InsFill, and training objectives remain unchanged. Equations (1)-(10) match. MinkowskiNet is added as an experimental backbone without a new augmentation component or procedural adaptation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same autonomous-driving semantic segmentation task on SemanticKITTI and nuScenes, with 19 and 16 classes respectively. Changes to labeling fractions and backbones concern experimental settings, not dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds DDSemi, LASS3D, IGNet, and LaserMix's range-view variant, while dropping ScribbleKITTI and CylinderMix from that comparison. CylinderMix joins the mixing-strategy comparison in Figure 6(c). The component-ablation reference also changes from MeanTeacher to supervision-only Cylinder3D.

E3.justification: v2 adds MinkowskiNet alongside Cylinder3D and restricts SemanticKITTI evaluation to 1%, 10%, 20%, and 50% labels, removing the 5% and 40% settings. Its component ablation reports a supervised-only control instead of MeanTeacher. These change the reported evaluation design; the PDFs do not establish that retained ablation configurations were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds qualitative error comparisons for three SemanticKITTI scenes, a training-time erased-point trajectory, and a class-probability case study (Figures 5, 6(b), and 7). Backbone adaptability is also examined. Existing component, mixing, and patch-split analyses remain; the dual-versus-multi-scene analysis moves from v1 Figure 5(b) to v2 Table 4.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v2's class-probability chart diagnoses individual predictions rather than introducing statistical uncertainty reporting for benchmark performance.

E6.justification: v2 Table 1 reports new AIScene results, including 61.2 and 63.4 mIoU at 1% labels on SemanticKITTI and nuScenes. The earlier Cylinder3D results, 54.5 and 56.6, remain unchanged in v2 Table 2; this is not an established same-setting gain. GPC's reported SemanticKITTI 10% score changes from 49.9 to 62.0. The ablation reference average changes from 55.4 to 54.5 while component scores remain unchanged. New comparator and diagnostic results are also added.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, pool definitions, EMA update, mixing equations, and loss definitions are mathematically unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contributions—point erasure for intra-scene consistency and multi-scene patch augmentation—remain. v2 explicitly extends the applicability claim to the whole segmentor-agnostic framework and foregrounds the independent usefulness of both erasure and augmentation.

C2.justification: v2 refines the mechanism explanation: ambiguous points interfere with pseudo-labeled-point feature learning, while augmentation complements erased scenes. It adds interpretations concerning small objects, boundaries, and sensitivity to scarce labels. The earlier qualification about LiM3D's different keyframe sampling is removed.

D1.justification: v2 identifies MinkowskiNet as an additional backbone and newly states that evaluation excludes ensembles and test-time augmentation. It removes the explicit assurance of LaserMix-identical sampling indices and uniform scene sampling. Hardware, spatial limits, thresholds, and loss weights remain documented as before. The omissions do not establish an actual sampling change.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands coverage of supervised segmentation architectures and recent semi-supervised research, explicitly positioning AIScene against density-based DDSemi, language-assisted LASS3D, and additional multimodal work. PointMixup and Pan et al.'s label-recommendation work disappear from the references. These changes exceed bibliographic reformatting.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, the method and title are renamed, and related work separates supervised and semi-supervised segmentation. Experimental discussion is substantially reorganized, with numbered sections and revised terminology throughout.

P2.justification: v2 redraws Figure 1, adds qualitative and probability figures, and combines retained plots with the new erasure trajectory in Figure 6. Dual/multi-scene bars become Table 4, and retained Cylinder3D results receive a separate table. Table 1 gains averages and improvement rows. The mismatched mixing/sensitivity captions in v1 are corrected.

improvement.justification: v2 provides a more informative assessment through current comparators, an additional backbone, diagnostic figures, clearer motivation, and corrected plot captions. The net gain is limited: sampling comparability is less explicit, and replacing MeanTeacher with a supervised-only ablation reference weakens attribution of component gains. The higher headline scores alone do not establish improvement under unchanged conditions.
